transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)

Position of the majority of young [sex of FGD] on the ladder of power and freedom (private rating): 5 = Power and freedom to make almost all major life decisions: 0 votes; 4 = Power and freedom to make many major life decisions: 2 votes; 3 = Power and freedom to make some major life decisions: 5 votes; 2 = Only a small amount of power and freedom: 3 votes; 1 = Almost no power or freedom to make decisions: 0 votes
I am married and married people decide together. I never decide by myself I will involve only in the discussion on major issues but my husband decides at the end

Most of the youth goes to school and we have very small amount of freedom to decide by ourselves. “I was 10th grade student when I got pregnant and the man who make me pregnant left me and my family blamed me for what I did and told me to stay home no more school or going out without their permission”. I never decide by myself since I made this mistake.

For me as a married couple it is always both of us who decide and I have the freedom to decide with my husband. I decide in small things but If we need to decide to sell land or big animals it is my husband who decide at the end. [If you refuse?] If I don’t agree with him he will kick me for sure.
Even if I went to school I have no right to decide because of this I couldnot get what I want.
Since we are under our family’s control it is our family who decide for us. They know what’s good for us.

As we differ in color our family’s are also different and one family may be free and give freedom for the kids to decide by themselves and some are giving decision for their kids in everything including who to marry.
Education is useful because we want to go out from this hopeless area not to remain here like the girls who married early (forced by their family) and becoming very poor and destitute.

Education is important it help us to know how to plan our family “I myself is remaining here as poor woman because I married early and dropped out from school. I really regret it [why would you mind sharing?] if I were not dropped out and continue my education I would be in a better place and my kids would have been in good places, with farming sometimes you find good harvest sometimes none, the poverty is higher than imagination”

Education is really important. “I don’t like to be a farmer it is really bad [why?] I never saw any body’s life changed because of farming it is always the same “my family’s family used to farm with Oxen still we farm with oxen never been improved”. I want to be government employee and leave this area as soon as possible.
Education is important and change people’s life. Only few people are improving their life through farming if they do other things aside otherwise farming take people down.
Both boys and girls reached 10th grade I mean majority.

[As I see here most of you here are below 10th grade why?] I dropped out because my father died when I was 9th grade and my mother is too poor to send me to the nearest town 8 km away .Paying for my accommodations and food was not possible for her and I was forced to drop out. I met my husband five years ago and I decided to marry him because that was the only solution for me to support my mother and me.

If it is education it should go as far as we go. I am from well off family my family allows me to run I am an athlete but they believe in education and I give more priority to my education. I want to go far up to University and I want to be an educated athlete.

Women in this area go up to 10th grade but boys dropped out from school in order to find job. Sometimes family forced girls to get married or to go to XX. They also forced the boys to get job and to support the family.

Both girls and boys should go at least till 10th grade. Even for the boys 10th grade is enough because they have the opportunity to work. For the girls either they go to XX or they get married. It is the girls/women who are always poor.
In this area parents try to educate both girls and boys. They would not discriminate

Over the year, parents have started saying education for girls is a curse because either they get pregnant or elope. “I myself fall to the wrong man ‘he was telling me he will marry me and make me happy’ when I got pregnant he run away and I forced to give birth in my parents’ house and I don’t blame them if they stop trusting me and my sisters”
Parents said “what’s the reason for the girl to go to school rather they prefer she married off and bring extra labor to them”

In our area parents encourage the boys to go to school. Unlike us boys if they do not want to go to school, he can marry whoever he chose and if he fights with his family also he will leave the house and go to find work or he can do whatever he want. If the girl refuses her parent’s wish she has nowhere to go and obey whatever they decide for her even if it is wrong.

Since child hood apart from our daily work in the household we also involve in all farming activities; weeding, cutting, harvesting and carrying.” Now with my husband I am responsible for the house hold chores and fully involved in the farm; including the actual plowing (with oxen and hoe).

School is half day here. We go to school in shifts I mean there are two shifts/day so whoever goes to school is at home in the afternoon and vice versa. During our free time we help our mothers in the house and in the farm.

Reasons for ending education
• Marriage
• Eloping with boys
• Losing parents
• Going to XX

Two most important reasons
• Marriage
• Eloping

It is marriage sometimes girls marry on their own will but most of the time they are forced by their family. For example I have 1 year and 8 months son that’s why I stay home and take care of my child, I brought lots of shame to my family and the father of my child is not supporting me.

Girls will involved in lots of things that will interfere in their education, they may get tricked by men when they go out from school, friends and middle men advice them wrongly to go to XX. Eloping and early pregnancy are also possible.
My goal was to graduate and becoming a nurse but my plans were aborted due to different reasons and now I am married and no longer able to get to school.

I am 16 years old but still 5th grade I lost both my family three years ago and then I was out of school to look after my younger brother and sisters. Now I returned to school and I want to be a doctor when I graduate.
I am at school and am also training as an athlete. I want to do both together my parents encourage me to do it. I mostly focus in my study and athletics.
I want to be a doctor and serve my village.
My wish was to be kebele administrator unfortunately I become sick and couldn’t pursue my education any more.
Tenth grade is mostly the highest grade for us girls; and when we finish school we often go to XX, or get married and stay home.
Mostly girls if their family affords it they prefer to go to XX. Some very few want to do some innovating work but they have no idea what to create or what to do.
Mostly parents spend lots of money thinking that if I send my daughter she can help herself and me. They don’t think that there is no way to work here and to be changed.
If there is vocational and technical schools that help them to get job.
It is better if they go to XX because it is easy to make money.

In my opinion most of the girls who went to XX coming back either sick or empty handed. These families who send their kids sell their cattle or borrow money from illegal lenders wishing their kids bring more. I suggest if they give this money to the kids to do things here or in the nearest town.

Most important for the [sex of the FGD] of the community (top 2)
• Improved heifers
• Poultry

Most important for the [opposite sex of FGD] of the community (top 2)
• Improved seeds
• Row planting
Improved heifers and chickens are the most that helps us because the butter, milk, cheese helps us to cover the day to day household consumption.
Since they get more crop and production men prefer row farming and improved seeds.

Here in our village if there is new technology or training it is the men will know about it first. Because they are closer to the agricultural extension agents; or reach people are the one who chose to be part of these important events. Women, Youth and poor are not always called to be part of it.
Women’s problem are wide there is no one remember to approach them especially if they are poor.
Module 2.  Gender norms, livelihoods, and family formation (1 ½ hours)

Important crops or livestock for [sex of FGD] Now
• vegetable garden
• poultry
• row planting

Important crops or livestock for [sex of FGD] Ten years ago
• vegetable garden
• poultry
In our case now and before 10 years we decide on small items sold and used for household consumption the rest land and big animals we have no right to decide.
The introduction of new technologies (such as row farming) fertilizer, pesticide and improved wheat seeds, beer barely…). Trainings on different technologies and women involvement in meetings

Women work in the house and farm but men only work on the farm this is the custom since long ago. For us the girls in school when we return home instead of doing our homework and study we help our mother in the house and when it is farming time we also work in the field.
When I come from school I feed the animals, prepare food, and collect water and wood. For my brothers they bring back the animals from field and go to study or play.

Men are not doing household chores because it is women’s job. If he does any work that we do, people will make joke and laugh at him. If a woman do men work like plowing land or anything it is ok. For example they will call him names ‘he is submissive’ ‘who is the man’ and ‘he should wear dress like her’

If it is in bulk especially he would sale it. I am not allowed to sell, if I do without his permission that is the end of me. Sometimes I sell small amount hiding from him to cover needs or household items.

In my parents case my father is the one who sell big animals including sheep, if my mother disagree with him I see him beating her “once because she said he can’t sell the cow she raised he beat her to death” If a woman did such thing she will be killed or send back to her family.
[Married] I know some people just take animals from the grazing land and sold in the market, when the wives find out, they will fight even divorce happened.

Here lands are held by men if the woman has land she must be widow, lost her husband or sometimes never gets married (inherited from family). Most of the time land is for men and they are the one who decided what to plant or not. Women have no knowledge like him on the issue.

As we already told you only one of them have land there is no women plot or men plot. The backyard farming also is assumed to be women’s in reality it is controlled by him. She only allowed to farm and plant small size of vegetables, beans and maize from which she ssale and use to fulfill household needs.

Women always work in the husband’s plots starting from plowing. Now days young couples work equal in their land “ I myself till the land with my husband the land for row planting farm 5-6 times, that is very hard and needs a lot of human power (4-5)”

Some men help women in their vegetable garden and allow her to sell the productions if it is not in bulk. If it is in bulk they (men) sell it while it is in the plot. Men are not selling small amount of vegetable in the market [why not] it is a shame even if the wife gets sick he ask/beg other women to sell them for him. He only sales in large quantity.

Women household heads and if they have no one to help them they give their land to share farming. The share farmer decided what to plant and how to farm and only give them portion of the produce as he wish (calculated the cost for the input he uses in the plot and his labor).
If the women household heads have children (boys) able to land they discuss with them and the men go to friends or development agents for advice.

Men are never discussing with women about their plots they rather go to friends, agricultural extension agents or do it without any advice. Women knows a lot about farming but never raised our voice because they get angry if we do. They may think that we are acting superior.
He will never allow her to join the group because he has already set his mind as a boss over her. And he will never allow her to mix with others.
He will tell her not to go. If she persists to do so there will be fight among them that will lead to may be divorce and obviously he will send her away empty handed.

Here the worst will come, since he don’t allow her to go out of the house, he might get violence and start beating her. He will say that “what you see outside do you have an affair” and he becomes suspicious and his friends and his family even might even encourage him to beat her or throw her out of his wife.
He will tell her that “I told you to eat whatever I give you” .

He will never ask her to rest the intention is to hold her in the house because if she have time to breath she might meet other people and know what’s going on with other women. A husband of my neighbor is similar to him he always wanted his wife to stay home and work with him, in the backyard and do all the work in the house like all the women in the area but never allow her to go out from the house, he even beats her if she says hello to other women in that area.

They will say that “do you have any responsibility to do work in the house while you have a wife” how come you send your wife away “she might meet somebody and cheat on you”. Some woman might envy her and will say how lucky she is having such a husband.
Both women and men will say to him “you lousy guy submissive for your wife, you are a woman not man”
They will say that “you better cut you penis and give it to her why you need it “and also when he go to bar or public areas they will call him woman.
On the other hand they will call the woman “greedy, street girl leaving her husband at home and roaming around” she make her husband a woman. She is the husband and he a wife (exchanging role)
She would be considered as witch who control him and put some evil things.
He will be disrespected by most of the people and only few might consider him as a normal person.
Men will ask him to stop treating his wife this way and even becoming violent and attack him in public areas. They will never allow their wives to be with her (even relatives of her and his)
He will be proud and will say I have strong wife better off.
If he is strong not affected by the comments and insults he will say that my wife is a model leave me alone.
He might be affected by all the comments from others and change his behavior.
Both men and women are born equally in nine months but in our society men becoming superior and women submissive that creates inequality.
Both men and women are equal.
There is no equality it is only talk “the bible said that men are the head of a woman” so that she should be under him. We are not equal.
Even if there is equality the man is a little higher than women because he is a husband he is on the top of woman. Even if equality is good husband is always the family head and bread winner.
There is no equality especially in our area we already saw that man make all the decision, women have no place to decide even in small things.
She will never decide by herself she might raise the issue of selling but at the end she needs to wait for her husband to do the final decision.
They might discuss and agree but if the request is from him at the end he will decide even if she disagrees she would have no choice.
They will decide together because there is law now days.
They will bring the issue to the table and discuss then decide together. If they want to sell or to eat it in the house they decide together.

If it is in bulk for sure he will sell it, if it in small amount it will be her since selling small amount of vegetable in the market is a shame for the man to sell “men would never sell cabbage” [everyone was laughing]

If the idea come from her he will never accept it or he will ask others like extension workers or friends as if the idea is his own and apply it once he got conformation but for sure he will tell for others it is his idea.
He will say “what do you know about this you are a woman”

She will not take any risk she is a woman if she lose there will be a lot of problem, this problem sometimes lead to physical violence or divorce. If she once loses her husband never trust her and everybody will point at her. That’s the reason we don’t want to take risk, even with our vegetable gardens.
Very difficult
Women never decide. It is his decision at the end of the day.

As far as the money is inherited it is her money even the law support her. However, it affects her relationship with her husband if she refuses. Most of the time this things lead to fight and violence.
It is very easy for him he is a man and the money is his. He can do whatever he wishes.
To start with if the girl is not married she is not allowed to walk in public areas and if she does she considered street girl she has no one to control her.
Married woman are going to the market to sell their vegetable, butter or other small items to the market and she go there to buy items she need.

Thanks to our government there is a road constructed and we go to the nearby market alone and if we want to go to the bigger market 8 km away from here we take taxi and go. So there is no problem. Previously before 5 years if we need to walk all the way, we needed to be accompanied by a man.
It is easy now days and easier we can go to the small market walking three times a week both to sell and to buy what we need.

For women with a husband it is him who is going to market (the big market) to sell big animals and to buy things. Regarding crop mostly our men sell for local store owners, farmers association and sometimes there are Isuzu trucks coming here. The farmers don’t need to go to the big market, the profit is only 10 birr and they prefer to sell it here.

For us women especially married if the husband allows us to go it is not difficult because there is taxi that only cost us two birr. For women headed household to sell her production in the big market by herself is not easy because there are thieves on the way who may steeltheir donkey and they can’t negotiate with the merchants in the market.

[You told us that it is easy for the women to move from place to place is it always safe for them?] No it is not always safe sometimes there are bad men attacking us, there is also abduction and rape, if she walk alone and most of the time we go with friends and men relatives. There is also no need to take short cuts through the forest. That is dangerous.

Out of every 10 women, how many move freely on their own in public spaces (private rating): 1 (practically no women move freely on their own in the village): 0 votes; 2: 0 votes; 3: 0 votes; 4: 0 votes; 5: 5 votes; 6: 1 vote; 7: 1 vote; 8: 0 votes; 9: 1 vote; 10 (practically all women move freely on their own in the village): 0 votes

I said five because comparing from the previous periods now it is really changed relatively women move freely even if there is some risks. The law also protected us somehow. Actually not always; because there is still discrimination. It is when our family are strong enough when the law serve better. There are also female police assigned.

Moving within our village has improved a little but going to other kebeles is still a problem. I remember that Young men from our adjacent kebele raped a married woman who went to visit her mother. No one tried to go to the police because there was no witness.
it is rather 2 we are still afraid of moving around in public areas because they give us names and we are afraid to be attacked when we walk alone
It is not easy unless the family send the girl child either to work for others or to relatives in the town for education purpose.

Many young girls are sent to XX for work. The family sometimes contracts their land, sell big animals or borrow money from illegal lenders to send them abroad. When the girls send back money, it is only very few family who save the money for them. other families use the money for themselves
[Do many young [sex of FGD] from here migrate?] Not anymore; there are some who try illegally. However, the legal route is closed by the government.

There are girls, who return from XX with good fortune; either they go back to work more or go to the near town open small shops. These women construct corrugated iron sheet house for their family, bought TV, fridge, sofa and improved heifers.

There are women returned with bad luck I mean, either they come mentally challenged, physically abused. People talk about them a lot and their family gets even poorer trying to return the money they spent to send their children abroad with. But still there are lots of women who are eager to go.

There are women who go to the nearest town for work [where and what kind of work?] house maid, waiter at a hotel or shops keeping. These women also built better houses for the family but in most cases they won’t return back unless for a visit.
Girls marry 15-18 and for boys it is 24 the minimum age to get married. [Among the eight participants two girls have children before marriage, three are students, and three are married]
They are the one who ask for marriage for the girls if she is lucky now days she get married early (15-18) our men are afraid of marriage because either they have no land or money.

Poverty forced us to drop out from school and to get married early as me “my father died when I was 15 (6th grade) and I have no one to support me our land is to small and my brother took over it, I met my husband and when he asked me to marry him when I was 16 years old I said Ok her I am poor with three kids”.
I was forced by my dad and got married when I was 16 years old and both our families gave us a Timad (¼ of a hectare) each.

There is marriage agreement between the boy and the girl. Still there is marriage among families that the boy chose a girl and asks his family (male) to go and to ask for her hand. Or the family chooses for him and bring for him. In Muslim society the man marries more than two wives.
There is also a kind of mistress a man can have a wife but still have another woman. If the wife died he is allowed to marry her sister or relatives especially in Muslim families.
As we already told you sometimes it is agreed between the boys and girls. Most of the times; it is the men who choose and decide.
There are women who gave birth when they are 13-14 (either married off by the family or raped) but mostly in our area we give birth when we reach at the age of 17-18.
[All said it is too early]
if I were not pregnant when I was too young I would be matured enough to decide whether I want to continued leaving with my husband or not.

Marriage at young age is bad we stopped our education, we get responsibility of the house, the husband on the top of these all having kids is not comfortable. No time to care for ourselves not alone for the kid, we have no idea how to take care of them.

I am 17 have a child (1year and 8 months) without marriage forced to drop out of school the father of the baby refused to support me. No job for me with the child therefore I am leaving with my family. My mom she is trying to help me but my father and brothers are still angry.
When she reached 20-23 because it is a good age she can be matured enough mentally and physically as she is no longer a child.
In my opinion having a child at early age is good because a child can protect you when grown up (especially if it is a boy) a girl is also ok if she is educated (she can support you financially).
If she is educated a little and have family planning training yes she could “for example I said 3 children are enough and told to my husband he agreed and I only have three kids”

Women in this area are using family planning programs through the health extension workers but still most women are under their husband’s control and if he say you have to get pregnant she do as much as she can. Some men even threaten the women if she doesn’t give him more children he will leave her.
Both the women and the husband are not deciding on how many children they will have or not it is God’s will.
Financial support made available for young boys and girls to do things other than farming.
Expansion of vocational training for all,
There is no credit scheme form the youth. If credit was made available for hem it could create better opportunities.
